header: Split 'train' of jev-cli-seed: a train-only seed corpus for the jev-cli domain (jev_factory.domains.jev_cli), agent-drafted on 2026-09-30 (plan task t33) and pending operator review before any teacher call (c68). It never goes to a val, test or held-out side: the split stage passes it as --train-only. Operation entries carry a phrasing class (imperative, question, terse, jargon, symptom); explain entries carry explain:<style> and a one-sentence answer; escalate entries carry decline:<reason> for the domain's eight reasons. Entries propose the verb only; every argument grounds against the world below (the CLI's own explain paths and stages). Written for this domain; no text is copied from another corpus.

What is a jev-like model?

expect.answer: A small calibrated scorer that reads one request and a lettered list of candidate actions and picks one with a single forward pass, including the explain and escalate controls.

entries.text: jev-like model, in one line?

expect.answer: A calibrated scorer that picks one of a bounded set of candidates, never a free-form generator.

entries.text: What does dry-run by default mean here?

expect.answer: Every write verb only reports what it would do unless you add --apply, which is what commits the change.

entries.text: Explain what --apply does.

expect.answer: --apply turns a write verb from a dry run into a real run that writes its artifacts; without it nothing on disk changes.

entries.text: What's the difference between a read-only and a mutating action?

expect.answer: A read-only action only reports; a mutating one changes state, so the gate holds it to stricter floor, margin and entropy thresholds.

entries.text: why does the gate have separate mutating thresholds?

expect.answer: Because a wrong mutating proposal costs more than a wrong read, the mutating floor, margin and max-entropy thresholds are stricter.

entries.text: What is expected calibration error?

expect.answer: ECE is the average gap between the model's stated confidence and its actual accuracy, weighted by how many predictions fall in each confidence bin.

entries.text: ECE?

expect.answer: Expected calibration error: how far confidence is from accuracy, averaged over bins; lower is better.

entries.text: What does temperature calibration do?

expect.answer: It divides the logits by one fitted temperature so the probabilities match observed accuracy, without changing which candidate is ranked first.

entries.text: when is the per-label calibration vector kept?

expect.answer: Only when it lowers ECE on the selection fold; otherwise temperature alone is used.

entries.text: Why is the held-out set sealed?

expect.answer: So it is touched only once, in the final measurement, and its numbers stay an honest estimate that no tuning decision has seen.

entries.text: I want to peek at held-out numbers mid-run, why is that not allowed?

expect.answer: Looking at the sealed set before the final run would let it influence decisions, so it is opened once, at the end, and never earlier.

entries.text: What's the difference between the fit fold and the selection fold?

expect.answer: The gate is fit on the fit fold only; the selection fold is kept apart to judge candidates against the pre-registered rule.

entries.text: fit fold vs selection fold?

expect.answer: Fit fold: where gate thresholds are fit. Selection fold: where candidates are compared. They never mix.

entries.text: What does pre-registration mean in this factory?

expect.answer: The bars and the selection rule are written and hashed before the first training command, so they cannot be tuned to the results.

entries.text: What is a recorded deviation?

expect.answer: An append-only record of a change to the plan, rule or bars after pre-registration, made instead of silently editing the original.

entries.text: can I just edit prereg.json after training started?

expect.answer: No; the registered file is locked by hash, and any later change has to be a recorded deviation.

entries.text: Why are arguments grounded outside the model?

expect.answer: The model only picks an action; argument values are matched deterministically against the world, so the model can never invent a target.

entries.text: Explain grounding in a sentence.

expect.answer: Grounding matches a request's argument to the one exact value the world snapshot lists, and declines when there is none or more than one.

entries.text: What is the permutation probe?

expect.answer: A test that reorders, re-letters, subsets and paraphrases the candidates to check the model's choice does not change with presentation.

entries.text: robustness bar?

expect.answer: The pick must survive reordering, re-lettering, subsetting and paraphrasing of the candidates.

entries.text: What is Q4_K_M?

expect.answer: A 4-bit GGUF quantization format; it is the deployed format, so it is the artifact that gets measured, not the bf16 checkpoint.

entries.text: the bf16 checkpoint scored great, why measure the quant again?

expect.answer: Because the quant is what ships and quantization can shift accuracy and calibration, so the shipped artifact is what gets measured.

entries.text: What does healing a quant mean?

expect.answer: One short extra fine-tune round on the same frozen set when quantization lost too much, done at most once.

entries.text: Why is publishing private-first?

expect.answer: Bundles are uploaded privately and verified by hash; making anything public is always a human decision and a hard stop.

entries.text: can the factory flip a bundle to public on its own?

expect.answer: No; going public is a human decision, never a factory step.

entries.text: What's the difference between explain and escalate?

expect.answer: Explain answers a knowledge question in words; escalate hands the request to a human or a more capable agent because no single listed action fits.

entries.text: explain vs escalate?

expect.answer: Explain: answer in words. Escalate: hand the request off.

entries.text: What does abstain_uncertain mean in a gate outcome?

expect.answer: The top candidate was not confident or clear enough to pass the gate, so the model abstains instead of proposing it.

entries.text: Why is only one GPU job run at a time?

expect.answer: Training and serving share the same accelerator and unified memory, so jobs run one at a time to avoid contention and crashes.

entries.text: What does the missing-candidate slice test?

expect.answer: Requests whose right action was removed from the candidate list, to check the model escalates instead of picking a wrong action.

entries.text: Tell me what leakage checking protects against.

expect.answer: It fails closed when a training entry exactly or nearly duplicates a protected test or held-out entry.

entries.text: Why do jev ask proposals never run anything?

expect.answer: ask only proposes a verb; a human or agent decides whether to run it, so a mutating verb is never executed by the model.

entries.text: what's a margin threshold in the gate?

expect.answer: The minimum gap between the top candidate's probability and the runner-up's before a proposal is allowed.

entries.text: What does max-entropy mean in the gate?

expect.answer: An upper limit on how spread out the candidate distribution may be; above it the model abstains.

entries.text: Why does the decider need a human gate to pick its successor?

expect.answer: To avoid circularity: a decider version never picks its own successor or trains on its own unconfirmed verdicts.

entries.text: what is a stage manifest?

expect.answer: The record each stage writes of its inputs and outputs, used to resume and to spot stale stages.

entries.text: What does resumable mean for a stage?

expect.answer: A killed stage restarts from where it stopped, reusing cached work instead of redoing it.

entries.text: Explain why the letters go A-Z then a-z.

expect.answer: Candidates are labelled with single letters, uppercase first then lowercase, giving at most 52 candidates per prompt.

entries.text: stock model scored terribly on baseline, is that normal?

expect.answer: Yes; a stock base model has never seen the lettered-candidate format, which is why the bars also include pre-registered absolute minimums.
